Cases.Purpose: Simplified Han, two individual partial glyph hits.
Traditional Han, two individual partial glyph hits.
Two source CIDs compose one Unicode kana grapheme; a base-only hit removes both.
One source CID maps to decomposed Hangul Jamo, rendered with precomposed 가 glyph; synthetic shaping-free mapping.
Supplementary CJK Extension B scalar remains an indivisible UTF-16 surrogate pair.
One source CID maps to Han plus supplementary variation selector; synthetic semantic mapping, not IVS font support.
One source CID maps to two Han scalars/graphemes; no geometric subdivision can safely remove only one.

Refusals.Reason: Only a single unrotated page is accepted.

Limitations: Benchmark-only restricted positive grammar: one page, horizontal Identity-H Type0 CIDFontType2, two-byte CIDs in Tj, identity text matrix, uniform size, no shaping, no TJ, clipping, marked content, forms or transforms. Every positive source uses a single packed Tj / native text pageobject, then splits retained glyphs into absolute matrices.

Unicode grapheme membership is read from actual ToUnicode. A source CID mapping to multiple scalars is indivisible even when it spans multiple graphemes; overlapping glyph clusters are merged transitively.

Kana combining uses separately positioned base/mark glyphs; Hangul decomposition, ideographic variation and multi-ideograph mappings are explicitly authored synthetic ToUnicode fixtures, not proof of OpenType shaping or real IVS glyph selection.

The complete licensed embedded TrueType program remains painting data; its general cmap and glyph outlines are not scrubbed. Unused document ToUnicode entries and removed CIDToGID entries are scrubbed.
Raw native fixture/geometry calls run strictly serially after singleton initialization; this is not a production queue, UI integration or cross-platform result.

Independent semantic/xref/font checks and Poppler target plus retained-pixel comparisons are required. Production partial text redaction remains unsupported until the parser and transaction integration are implemented.

partialImageRedaction.Algorithm: Affine pixel-cell polygon intersection; positive overlap replaces every component by 255; invocation-private image; public RemoveAllNonPageData full rewrite.

Limitations: Authored 32x24 lossless DeviceRGB or DeviceGray 8-bit images and page-level q/Q/cm/Do only; arbitrary content and nested Forms are refused.
JPEG/JPX/JBIG2, image masks, soft masks, Decode arrays, clipping, transparency, singular transforms and non-default page geometry are refused before mutation.
Intersecting pixel cells are erased conservatively, including their portions outside the region. Exact subpixel vector boundaries require resampling and a separate quality policy.
Shared unselected invocations intentionally retain original visible pixels. The erasure claim is scoped to the selected invocation, not global absence of a repeated image.
The experiment proves pixel-sample removal and immutable original input, not filesystem history erasure, production selection/UI, Linux qualification, throughput or arbitrary-PDF compatibility.
